profile.reading: Ark Duluth Data Center, per the operator's own site, sits at 3401 Technology Drive, Duluth, Minnesota 55811, in St. Louis County, and totals more than 26,000 square feet with 10,000 square feet of conditioned data center space, 300 racks available, and 1,000 kilowatts of power capacity. The operator's own site states the facility earned Energy Star certification for a fifth consecutive year as of 2023. This building is one of two distinct Duluth facilities the operator maintains per an independent data center industry aggregator directory, the other being Duluth 2 at 421 North 6th Avenue East, Duluth, Minnesota 55805, which is not the subject of this specific registry row. This row's address was applied after a third party reverse geocode of its own stored coordinates returned an exact, maximum confidence match to the Duluth 1 address, corroborating the aggregator's own name specific listing. A third, differing address found in a separate aggregator listing, 4361 Rice Lake Road, matched neither known Duluth building nor this row's coordinates and was not applied, noted here as a likely stale or inaccurate aggregator entry rather than treated as fact. Ark Data Centers, per its own about page, was founded in 2007 as a Tier III edge data center provider and now operates purpose built, owned and operated facilities across eight markets including Arizona, Idaho, Iowa, Minnesota, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin, of which this Duluth building is part of the Minnesota market. Company wide certifications listed on Ark's own site include HITRUST CSF, PCI, NIST, HIPAA, ITAR, and ITIL. This registry row previously confirmed this brand is the current name for the former Involta brand in this Minnesota market as well, unrelated in ownership history to the separate, larger batch of former Involta facilities this registry tracks in Ohio, though now under the same corrected Ark Data Centers operator name.

reading.body:
Ark Duluth Data Center holds 300 racks across 10,000 square feet of conditioned space, drawing 1,000 kW of IT power. Assuming 3.3 kW per rack, a density typical of older enterprise colocation, this translates to roughly 300 racks of compute capacity. The facility is Energy Star certified as of 2023, qualifying it for efficient operation at that specification tier.

Minnesota has published power capacity at only 2 of 13 mapped data center facilities. Ark Duluth's 1 megawatt ranks second in the state among published figures, behind a 9 megawatt facility, and represents 10 percent of the state's total published data center capacity. No information on Minnesota's grid constraints or wholesale power access is published here.

This campus is too small to drive AI scaling decisions. A thousand kilowatts places it outside the emerging density tiers that matter for large language model training, where individual facilities now routinely exceed 100 megawatts. It serves regional colocation demand, a category disconnected from the accelerator procurement pipelines that consume grid capacity at scale.
